content.user_title: Diagnose Ad Fatigue Before Scaling Spend
content.value_statement: Rising frequency and falling engagement can waste advertising budget. This skill compares trend data with an early baseline to recommend a clear next action.
actual_capabilities: Compares current frequency, CTR, CVR, and reach with an early-flight baseline.
Distinguishes creative fatigue from audience saturation using trend patterns.
Returns Rotate-creative, Widen-audience, or Hold for each ad set.
Flags unreliable conversion tracking before making CVR-based decisions.
Labels figures as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
limitations: Requires a daily or weekly time series for a reliable fatigue assessment.
Does not create replacement advertisements or new audience segments.
Does not calculate account quality scores or apply account vetoes.
Cannot verify platform data or conversion tracking without supplied exports.

use_cases.title: Review declining campaign engagement
use_cases.description: Assess whether a scaling prospecting ad set needs fresh creative or a broader audience.

use_cases.title: Prepare a budget scaling decision
use_cases.description: Use frequency and conversion trends to decide whether an ad set can scale safely.

use_cases.title: Check agency campaign reports
use_cases.description: Review exported campaign data and identify where tracking uncertainty limits a recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Basic fatigue check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this ad set. Frequency rose from 2.1 to 4.8 and CTR fell from 1.4% to 0.8%. Should I rotate creative, widen the audience, or hold?

prompt_templates.title: Analyze an export
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this daily ad-set export against its early-flight baseline. Return frequency, CTR, CVR, reach trends, diagnosis, trigger, and caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Compare several ad sets
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these ad sets over four weeks. Give one trigger per set and explain the threshold or trend that caused it.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a conversion decline
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this campaign for fatigue. Compare platform CVR with my GA4 order export and flag tracking risks before recommending an action.

output_examples.input: Frequency increased from 2.0 to 5.1, CTR declined by 42%, and reach continued growing.
output: Reason: Frequency increased while CTR declined and reach kept growing.
Caveat: Confirm the conversion trend before changing budget.

output_examples.input: Reach plateaued, frequency rose from 3.2 to 6.0, and CTR and CVR both declined.
output: Reason: The reachable audience appears exhausted.
Caveat: Validate conversion tracking against order data.

best_practices: Provide daily or weekly exports that include impressions, reach, frequency, CTR, CVR, and spend.
Identify the stable period after learning phase as the baseline window.
Validate CVR changes with order or analytics data before taking action.
anti_patterns: Do not diagnose fatigue from a single day of campaign data.
Do not use one universal frequency threshold for every campaign objective.
Do not treat estimated audience saturation as a measured fact.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a daily or weekly export with impressions, reach, frequency, clicks or CTR, conversions or CVR, and spend.

faq.question: Can I use a single-day screenshot?
faq.answer: No. The skill needs a trend over time and an early-flight baseline.

faq.question: What causes a Rotate-creative result?
faq.answer: It usually indicates rising frequency and declining CTR while reach is still growing.

faq.question: What causes a Widen-audience result?
faq.answer: It usually indicates a reach plateau, rising frequency, and weakening engagement or conversion metrics.

faq.question: Does this skill create new advertisements?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses the issue and can recommend a creative-building skill next.

faq.question: How does it handle uncertain tracking?
faq.answer: It flags unreliable conversion data and avoids using it as the basis for a final fatigue decision.
